chapter: Rhythm Club memories and playing technique
title: Ward Pinkett and Louis Metcalf

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well when I was reading the discography there, I remember so many of the names, Ward Pinkut for one, trumpet player.

That's right, and he was a very good trumpet player. And I remember him, oh he and I had some wonderful discussions at the Band Box, the Rhythm Club, and we were on several other record dates, I just forget. But I do remember the ones that we did with Jelly Roll, and I liked his playing very much. Ward Pinkett, he died quite young.
Died of pneumonia. Did you have much association with him after you were with Jelly Roll?
No, not too much, only off and on seeing him at the club, he and I would have coffee together, talk about different sessions. Things like that, different musicians.
What kind of a person was he?

He was very calm, very nice, unassuming, you know and just was very nice, had a very nice personality. Very nice personality, and seemed to have a lot of friends. And of course he was very popular in the recording field because other than Jelly he was making records with quite a few different guys around, you know.
Well such as Frank Newton, I think he doubled there with Frankie Newton on some of the sides if I'm not mistaken, I'm not sure. Then let's see, who did he record with?
Let's see, according to Chilton he was with Rex Stewart's band, Earl McGee's orchestra, Teddy Hill, Albert Nicholas and Bernard Addison, and Louis Metcalf band.
Yeah, well I was mistaken then about what was the other name.
Yeah, it wasn't with Frankie Newton, it was with those bands that you just mentioned. Louie Metcalf, I know that I was thinking of a trumpet player, Louie Metcalf.
He's still very much with us, right?
Oh yeah, yeah, Louie Metcalf is still living. I haven't seen him in a few years, but I understand he's still gigging around New York.
